Sub-issue of #123 (priority 2 of 5 — read-only survey, no destructive code path exists yet). Mirrors the pattern proved by #112 -> #122.

## Symptom (fact)

`.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml` (originated by #31, see retro #104) carries ~180 lines of inline bash across two steps (`Survey candidate branches`, `Maintain rolling summary issue`) that:

1. Validate `dry_run` (boolean) and `min_age_days` (non-negative integer) inputs.
2. Walk every branch from `gh api --paginate /repos/${REPO}/branches`, parse last-commit dates, compute age in days, filter out (a) the default branch, (b) anything newer than `min_age_days`, (c) anything with an open PR.
3. Write rows to both `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and `/tmp/cleanup-comment.md`.
4. Reconcile against a rolling summary issue: create if missing-and-candidates>0; append comment if exists-and-candidates>0; auto-close if existing-but-idle ≥ 28 days; silent otherwise.

The candidate-filter algebra and the 5-row state table of the rolling-issue lifecycle (#104's table) are the kind of logic that pytest excels at — but right now they live as `gh` shell-outs and `date -u -d ... +%s` arithmetic that can only be smoke-tested in CI.

## Scope of fix

### `scripts/branch_cleanup.py` (new)

Pure functions (no I/O):
- `parse_dry_run(raw: str) -> bool` — accepts `"true"`/`"false"`, raises `ValueError` otherwise.
- `parse_min_age_days(raw: str) -> int` — non-negative integer, raises `ValueError` otherwise.
- `is_candidate(*, branch: str, default_branch: str, last_commit_utc: datetime, now_utc: datetime, min_age_days: int, has_open_pr: bool) -> bool` — the four-condition filter.
- `format_summary_row(branch: str, last_commit_utc: datetime, age_days: int, sha: str) -> str` — Markdown table row.
- `decide_issue_action(*, candidate_count: int, existing_issue: dict | None, idle_seconds: int, idle_threshold_seconds: int) -> Literal["create", "append", "close", "silent"]` — the 5-row state table from #104.

Side-effect wrappers (mockable):
- `list_branches(repo: str, *, runner=subprocess.run) -> list[tuple[str, str]]` — `gh api --paginate /repos/.../branches`.
- `get_last_commit_date(repo: str, sha: str, *, runner=subprocess.run) -> datetime`.
- `count_open_prs_for_head(repo: str, branch: str, *, runner=subprocess.run) -> int`.
- `find_rolling_issue(repo: str, title: str, *, runner=subprocess.run) -> dict | None`.
- `comment_on_issue(...)`, `create_issue(...)`, `close_issue_with_comment(...)`.

CLI:
- `python3 scripts/branch_cleanup.py survey --repo OWNER/NAME --dry-run BOOL --min-age-days N --default-branch BRANCH` — writes summary table to stdout, writes per-row comment file to `--out PATH`, prints candidate count to stderr.
- `python3 scripts/branch_cleanup.py reconcile --repo OWNER/NAME --title TITLE --candidate-count N --comment-file PATH --idle-close-days 28` — implements the 5-row state machine.

### `tests/test_branch_cleanup.py` (new, target: ~35 cases)

- `TestParseDryRun` / `TestParseMinAgeDays` — happy + every reject case.
- `TestIsCandidate` — default-branch excluded; age below threshold excluded; open-PR excluded; all-clear included; boundary at exactly `min_age_days` (the existing `>` semantic must be preserved).
- `TestFormatSummaryRow` — SHA truncation to 7 chars, ISO date pass-through.
- `TestDecideIssueAction` — every cell of the 5-row state table from #104, plus the boundary at exactly 28 days.
- `TestListBranches` — pagination handling (mock 2 pages), empty repo (no branches), single branch.
- `TestGetLastCommitDate` — parses GitHub's ISO-8601 with `Z` suffix; `+00:00` form; raises on malformed.
- `TestCountOpenPrsForHead` — 0, 1, many.
- `TestCLI survey` — empty repo prints `Total branches: 0`, candidate_count=0; single old orphan listed; old branch with open PR excluded.
- `TestCLI reconcile` — every state-machine outcome end-to-end with monkeypatched gh stubs.

### `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml`

Both inline shell steps collapse to single Python invocations. Idle-close threshold stays as `IDLE_CLOSE_DAYS: "28"` env var (passed through `--idle-close-days`).

### `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`

`lint-uv-pin` (or its successor `lint-scripts` once we hit rule of three) gains a step running this module's pytest.

## Out of scope

- **Goal D from #31** — adding the actual delete code path. This refactor preserves the read-only behaviour; widening to `contents: write` + `gh api DELETE` is its own issue per #104's deferred verification.
- Changing the rolling-issue auto-close threshold (28 days), the label set (`layer:meta` + `type:docs`), or the title format.
- Switching from `gh` CLI to PyGithub.

## Verify

- `uv run --group dev pytest tests/test_branch_cleanup.py -v` passes locally.
- `gh workflow run branch-cleanup.yml --ref main -f dry_run=true -f min_age_days=60` produces an identical `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` shape to the pre-refactor run (compare via the run UI).
- Forced-hit edge: `-f min_age_days=0` opens (or appends to) the rolling issue exactly as #104 documents.
- Empty default golden path: silent on no candidates, matches `Empty run, no open rolling issue. Silent.` log line.

## Refs

- Parent tracking: #123
- Pattern precedent: #112 -> #118 + #122.
- Workflow origin: #31; retro: #104; PR that delivered: #101.
- CLAUDE.md §3 — deterministic harness; §4 — minimum code, fail loudly on invalid input.

Sub-issue of #123 (priority 3 of 5 — read-only detection; opens issues only, no live writes). Mirrors the pattern proved by #112 -> #122.

## Symptom (fact)

`.github/workflows/ruleset-drift.yml` (originated by #30, delivered by #116) carries ~190 lines of inline bash across `Diff SoT vs live and detect unknown rulesets` + two `gh issue create` steps that:

1. Walk every SoT file in `.github/rulesets/*.json`; for each, fetch the matching live ruleset via `GET /repos/.../rulesets/{id}` and `diff -u` the canonical projection (`{name, target, enforcement, conditions, bypass_actors, rules}`).
2. Classify each into `in-sync` / `missing-on-live` / `drift` / `ambiguous` (multiple live rulesets with the same name -> abort).
3. Detect "unknown" rulesets (live name not present in SoT name set) via jq set difference.
4. Emit two structured issue bodies — one for SoT-vs-live drift, one for unknown rulesets — each with summary table, per-ruleset diff blocks, and a remediation section.
5. File issues only when the corresponding count > 0, with specific labels (`layer:meta` + `type:fix`).

The classification logic and the issue-body composition are pure transformations of JSON inputs to Markdown outputs. They cannot be unit-tested today; the only signal is whether a real cron run produces a sensible issue.

## Scope of fix

### `scripts/ruleset_drift.py` (new)

Pure functions:
- `classify(sot: dict, live_rulesets: list[dict]) -> dict` — returns `{"status": "in-sync"|"missing-on-live"|"drift"|"ambiguous", "live_id": int|None, "match_count": int}` for one SoT entry.
- `canonical_projection(ruleset: dict) -> dict` — returns the comparable subset `{name, target, enforcement, conditions, bypass_actors, rules}` sorted.
- `diff_canonical(sot: dict, live: dict) -> str` — unified-diff string (delegates to `difflib.unified_diff`, since stdlib gives byte-equivalent output to `diff -u`).
- `find_unknown(sot_names: list[str], live: list[dict]) -> list[dict]` — set difference returning `{id, name, target, enforcement}` tuples.
- `render_sot_drift_issue(*, run_url: str, run_date: str, repo: str, rows: list[dict], diffs: list[tuple[str, int, str]]) -> str` — full Markdown body.
- `render_unknown_issue(*, run_url: str, run_date: str, unknowns: list[dict]) -> str` — full Markdown body.
- `render_summary_section(rows: list[dict], header: str) -> str` — shared Markdown table renderer for `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.

Side-effect wrappers (mockable):
- `fetch_live_rulesets_list(repo: str, token: str, *, opener=urllib.request.urlopen) -> list[dict]` — `GET /repos/.../rulesets`.
- `fetch_live_ruleset(repo: str, ruleset_id: int, token: str, *, opener=...) -> dict`.
- `file_issue(repo: str, title: str, body_file: Path, labels: list[str], *, runner=subprocess.run) -> None`.

CLI:
- `python3 scripts/ruleset_drift.py detect --repo OWNER/NAME --sot-dir .github/rulesets --run-url URL --summary-file PATH --sot-body-file PATH --unknown-body-file PATH` — does the read + classify + render, writes summary + issue bodies to the named files, prints `drift_count` and `unknown_count` to stdout (for `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`).
- `python3 scripts/ruleset_drift.py file-sot-issue --repo OWNER/NAME --run-date YYYY-MM-DD --body-file PATH` — `gh issue create` wrapper.
- `python3 scripts/ruleset_drift.py file-unknown-issue --repo OWNER/NAME --run-date YYYY-MM-DD --body-file PATH` — ditto.

### `tests/test_ruleset_drift.py` (new, target: ~40 cases)

- `TestClassify` — in-sync, missing-on-live, drift (one field differs), drift (rules differ in order — must still drift), ambiguous (2 matches).
- `TestCanonicalProjection` — only the 6 fields kept; sort-stability across rules list; ignores live-only metadata (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, etc.).
- `TestDiffCanonical` — empty diff returns empty string; field-rename produces +/- pair; rules-list reorder shows up as diff (which is the intended behaviour today).
- `TestFindUnknown` — empty live, all-known, single unknown, multiple unknowns, names with special chars (URL-encode-safe).
- `TestRenderSotDriftIssue` — header includes `Parent: #30`, run URL, RUN_DATE; table has correct columns; `Diffs` section appears only when ≥1 drift row; `Remediation` section literal preserved.
- `TestRenderUnknownIssue` — header includes `Parent: #30`; "Unknown rulesets" table; remediation links to `docs/rulesets.md` rollback section.
- `TestFetchLiveRulesetsList` — happy path; auth header included; 401 raises with descriptive message.
- `TestFetchLiveRuleset` — same.
- `TestFileIssue` — labels passed through; body-file existence asserted; subprocess args validated.
- `TestCLI detect` — clean tree (drift=0, unknown=0); SoT drift only; unknown only; both; ambiguous live causes non-zero exit.

### `.github/workflows/ruleset-drift.yml`

Three inline shell steps collapse to three Python invocations. `RULESETS_PAT` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` env vars unchanged.

### `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`

`lint-uv-pin` job (likely renamed to `lint-scripts` by this point — third sub-issue passes the rule of three threshold) gains a step running this module's pytest.

## Out of scope

- Changing the cron schedule (`0 21 * * 0`) or the issue labels.
- Adding auto-remediation (the issue's `Remediation` section stays a human-actionable runbook link).
- Tightening the canonical projection (e.g. ignoring rule-list order). #30 / #116 considered this and intentionally rejected it; preserve behaviour.

## Verify

- `uv run --group dev pytest tests/test_ruleset_drift.py -v` passes locally.
- `gh workflow run ruleset-drift.yml --ref main` produces identical `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` shape to a pre-refactor run.
- Negative test: stage a one-field drift in `.github/rulesets/main.json` on a throwaway branch, force a dispatch -> exactly one SoT-drift issue filed, body matches snapshot.
- Negative test: stage an unknown live ruleset (via dispatch of `apply-rulesets.yml` with a name not in SoT — gate by environment first), confirm exactly one unknown-ruleset issue filed.

## Refs

- Parent tracking: #123
- Pattern precedent: #112 -> #118 + #122.
- Workflow origin: #30; delivered by #116.
- Sibling concern: #120 (PR-time `required_status_checks` sync — orthogonal axis).
- CLAUDE.md §3 — deterministic detector; §4 — abort loudly on ambiguous duplicates.

Sub-issue of #123 (priority 4 of 5 — first mutating workflow; gated by `environment: ruleset-apply`). Mirrors the pattern proved by #112 -> #122.

## Symptom (fact)

`.github/workflows/apply-rulesets.yml` (originated by #18) carries ~170 lines of inline bash across `Plan and apply rulesets` + `Enable auto-delete head branches` + `Auto-delete (dry-run plan)` that:

1. Map the `ruleset` input choice (`all-branches`/`main`/`both`) to a list of SoT files.
2. Fetch live rulesets via `GET /repos/.../rulesets`; classify each SoT file as POST-new vs PUT-update vs ambiguous (multiple matches -> abort).
3. For PUT cases, fetch the existing live body and emit a `diff -u` block in the step summary.
4. Apply via POST or PUT with a hand-rolled 3-attempt retry loop (5xx + curl-level "000" only; 4xx breaks early).
5. Toggle `delete_branch_on_merge` repo setting via PATCH; emit before/after status.

This is the **first mutating** workflow in this refactor strategy. The retry logic and the POST/PUT decision are pure transformations of inputs; the diff rendering is `difflib.unified_diff`. Today none of it can be unit-tested.

## Scope of fix

### `scripts/rulesets_apply.py` (new)

Pure functions:
- `select_targets(choice: Literal["all-branches", "main", "both"]) -> list[str]` — returns the ordered list of SoT filenames.

Sub-issue of #123 (priority 5 of 5 — most mutating, densest reconciliation logic; do last). Mirrors the pattern proved by #112 -> #122.

## Symptom (fact)

`.github/workflows/apply-labels.yml` (originated by #34/#84) carries ~160 lines of inline bash in `Plan and apply labels` that:

1. Fetch live labels via `GET /repos/.../labels?per_page=100` (with a hard fail if `length >= 100` — pagination not implemented).
2. Pass 1 — for each SoT label, compare against live: POST if missing; PATCH if color or description differs; no-op if both match.
3. Pass 2 — for each live label not in SoT: report-only when `prune=false`; DELETE when `prune=true` (and `dry_run=false`).
4. All API calls go through an inlined `apply_call()` shell function with a 3-attempt retry, exponential backoff (`ATTEMPT * 5`), 4xx-breaks-early, 5xx-retries semantic — **a structural duplicate** of `apply-rulesets.yml`'s retry block.
5. Step-summary table generated row-by-row with per-row action + diff annotations + HTTP code or `dry-run` placeholder.

The reconciliation algebra (POST vs PATCH vs no-op vs DELETE-or-skip) is the most intricate of all five workflows — and the retry helper is the third call site (after `ruleset-drift` fetch + `rulesets-apply` apply), which crosses the **rule-of-three threshold** for extracting a shared `scripts/_github_api.py` helper (per #123's "Risks" section).

## Scope of fix

### `scripts/labels_apply.py` (new)

Pure functions:
- `validate_sot(sot: list[dict]) -> None` — asserts every entry has `name` (str, non-empty), `color` (hex), `description` (str, ≤100 chars); raises `ValueError` with the offending name on failure (mirrors the existing `description | length > 100` jq check).
- `decide_label_action(*, sot_entry: dict, live_entry: dict | None) -> dict` — returns `{"action": "POST"|"PATCH"|"NOOP", "method": str, "url_suffix": str, "payload": dict | None, "color_changed": bool, "desc_changed": bool}`.
- `decide_prune_action(*, live_name: str, in_sot: bool, prune: bool, dry_run: bool) -> Literal["skip", "report", "plan-delete", "delete"]`.
- `render_action_row(name: str, action: str, color_changed: str, desc_changed: str, result: str) -> str`.

Side-effect wrappers (mockable):
- `fetch_live_labels(repo: str, token: str, *, opener=urllib.request.urlopen) -> list[dict]` — includes the `length >= 100` guard with the documented error message.
- `apply_call(*, method: str, url: str, payload: dict | None, token: str, opener=..., sleeper=time.sleep) -> tuple[int, str]` — **moved into `scripts/_github_api.py` as a shared helper** (rule of three crossed; see #123 Risks); imported by `labels_apply.py` and `rulesets_apply.py`. Behaviour byte-identical to the bash version: 3 attempts, sleep `ATTEMPT * 5`, retry on 5xx/`000`, break on 4xx.

CLI:
- `python3 scripts/labels_apply.py plan --repo OWNER/NAME --sot .github/labels.json --prune BOOL --summary-file PATH` — read + classify + render; no live writes.
- `python3 scripts/labels_apply.py apply --repo OWNER/NAME --sot .github/labels.json --prune BOOL --summary-file PATH` — plan + write; preserves exit-on-first-failure semantic.

### `scripts/_github_api.py` (new — extracted from this sub-issue, also imported by `rulesets_apply.py`)

Single function: `apply_call(...)` per the signature above. Tests live in `tests/test_github_api.py` (covers retry behaviour exhaustively so neither caller needs to repeat it). The earlier sub-issue (#4 — apply-rulesets) ships an inline copy; this sub-issue's PR replaces both call sites with the shared import as part of its diff.

### `tests/test_labels_apply.py` (new, target: ~45 cases)

- `TestValidateSot` — happy path; missing name; missing color; description over 100 chars (must surface offending name in the error).
- `TestDecideLabelAction` — POST when live is None; PATCH when color differs; PATCH when description differs; PATCH when both differ; NOOP when both match; empty live description treated as `""` (matches current `// ""` fallback).
- `TestDecidePruneAction` — every cell of the `(in_sot, prune, dry_run)` truth table.
- `TestRenderActionRow` — pipe-escape in label names; HTTP code formatting; em-dash placeholders for irrelevant cells.
- `TestFetchLiveLabels` — happy path; `length >= 100` triggers documented error; auth header included.
- `TestCLI plan` — all-new SoT (3 POSTs planned); mixed POST/PATCH/NOOP; pruning planned when `prune=true`; pruning suppressed when `prune=false` (report-only row).
- `TestCLI apply` — assert correct method/URL/payload per row via mocked `apply_call`; first failure aborts subsequent rows.
- `TestCLI apply with prune` — DELETE issued for live-not-in-SoT entries.

### `tests/test_github_api.py` (new — covers the shared helper)

- `TestApplyCall happy 2xx` — single attempt; sleeper not called.
- `TestApplyCall retry 5xx -> 5xx -> 2xx` — sleeper called with `5, 10`.
- `TestApplyCall break on 4xx` — single attempt; returns the 422 immediately; no retry.
- `TestApplyCall curl-level "000"` — retries up to 3 attempts.
- `TestApplyCall all attempts fail` — returns the final code; caller responsible for exit.
- `TestApplyCall payload None vs dict` — both forms produce correct request body.

### `.github/workflows/apply-labels.yml`

The 160-line `Plan and apply labels` step collapses to two Python invocations (plan + apply, or just `apply` which internally plans-then-writes). `Validate labels.json JSON syntax` and `Validate labels.json description length` shell steps fold into `labels_apply.py validate` (or stay as `jq` one-liners — operator choice).

### `.github/workflows/apply-rulesets.yml`

Replace the inline `apply_call` block from sub-issue #4 with `from _github_api import apply_call`. This is the **only** behavioural-equivalent change to that workflow in this PR.

### `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`

`lint-scripts` job (already renamed by sub-issue #3 or #4) gains both `tests/test_labels_apply.py` and `tests/test_github_api.py`.

## Out of scope

- Adding pagination to `fetch_live_labels` (the current `length >= 100` guard already surfaces the limit loudly per CLAUDE.md §4; pagination is a separate concern, file if/when the label count actually approaches 100).
- Changing retry backoff or attempt count.
- Re-shaping the SoT JSON.

## Verify

- `uv run --group dev pytest tests/test_labels_apply.py tests/test_github_api.py -v` passes locally.
- Dispatch `apply-labels.yml` with `dry_run=true, prune=false` — `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` matches pre-refactor shape exactly.
- Dispatch with `dry_run=true, prune=true` — additional `report-only` rows convert to `plan-only (DELETE)` rows.
- Dispatch with `dry_run=false, prune=false` against a no-op SoT — every row shows `unchanged`; no API writes recorded in the run log.
- Negative test: introduce a SoT entry with `description` length 101 chars — fails the validate step before any API call.
- Negative test: stub a 503 response for one POST — retry logic kicks in (visible in the step log), final state matches a 2xx happy path.

## Refs

- Parent tracking: #123
- Pattern precedent: #112 -> #118 + #122.
- Workflow origin: #34 (`agent:*` retired) -> #84 (current label taxonomy).
- Companion: this PR refactors the structural retry duplicate that sub-issue #4 first introduces; sub-issue #4 may merge with the duplicate, and this PR consolidates.
- CLAUDE.md §3 — harness; §4 — fail loudly on validation, preserve `dry_run` + `environment:` gates; §5 — rule of three (3 call sites = extract shared helper).

## Context

`.github/workflows/verify-issue-link.yml` carries ~30 LOC of inline bash that strips HTML comments from a PR body, regex-extracts `Refs|Closes|Fixes|Resolves #N` references, and verifies each `#N` resolves via `gh api`. Per #123, inline YAML shell is untestable and violates CLAUDE.md section 3 (deterministic harness). #112 -> #122 established the precedent: pure logic moves to `scripts/*.py` with pytest coverage; the workflow shells out to the entry point.

This sub-issue is first in #123's priority order because it is the smallest (~30 LOC), read-only (no GitHub writes), and the side-effect surface is a single `gh api` GET — the lowest blast-radius candidate to iterate the testing pattern on.

## Scope of fix

Mirrors `scripts/uv_pin.py` + `tests/test_uv_pin.py` shape.

1. New `scripts/issue_link.py` with pure functions and an argparse CLI:
   - `strip_html_comments(body: str) -> str` -- Python equivalent of `perl -0777 -pe 's///gs'` using `re.sub` with DOTALL + non-greedy.
   - `extract_refs(body: str) -> list[int]` -- case-insensitive multiline match of `^\s*(Refs|Closes|Fixes|Resolves)\s+#(\d+)`, sorted-unique ints. Composes with `strip_html_comments` so HTML-commented refs are not picked up.
   - `issue_exists(repo: str, number: int) -> bool` -- thin `subprocess.run(["gh", "api", f"/repos/{repo}/issues/{number}", "--silent"])` wrapper; returns False on any subprocess failure (mirrors `uv_pin.fetch_latest_uv_release()` pattern).
   - CLI: `python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo "$REPO"` reads `PR_BODY` from env (matches the workflow's existing contract), prints `OK: #N resolves...` / `::error::Referenced #N does not exist...` / `::error::PR body has no issue reference...`, exits 0 or 1.

2. New `tests/test_issue_link.py` covering:
   - `strip_html_comments`: empty body, no comments, single-line comment, multi-line comment, multiple comments, comment containing the keyword (must not survive into `extract_refs`).
   - `extract_refs`: each keyword case-insensitively (`refs`, `REFS`, `Refs`, `Closes`, `Fixes`, `Resolves`), single ref, multiple refs (sorted-unique), leading whitespace allowed, mid-line `Refs #5` rejected (anchor `^`), `Reference #5` rejected (word boundary on keyword), HTML-commented ref skipped after composition, no refs found.
   - `issue_exists`: success (return True), `subprocess.CalledProcessError` non-zero (False), `FileNotFoundError` (False), `TimeoutExpired` (False) -- monkeypatched per `test_uv_pin.TestFetchLatestUvRelease`.
   - CLI: happy path with one resolvable ref, no refs (exit 1, `::error::` message), one resolvable + one missing (exit 1), missing `PR_BODY` env (exit 1 or treat as empty -- decide during impl).

3. `.github/workflows/verify-issue-link.yml` collapses to a single `python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo "$REPO"` step. Inline LOC drops from ~30 to under 10 (just the step shell-out + env marshalling).

4. `verify-agents.yml` already runs `python3 -m pytest -v`; `tests/test_issue_link.py` is auto-picked up via `testpaths = ["tests"]` in `pyproject.toml`. No new CI wiring needed (#112 already paved that path).

## Out of scope

- Behaviour change. Same exit codes, same `::error::` annotation strings, same stdout (modulo Python-vs-bash formatting if it matches the spec literally).
- Migrating to PyGithub / githubkit (#123: stdlib + subprocess preferred until a sub-issue's tests outgrow that).
- Shared HTTP retry helper. `issue_exists` does a single GET, so no retry logic exists to deduplicate yet -- rule of three (#123).
- The other 4 sub-issues of #123 (branch-cleanup, ruleset-drift, apply-rulesets, apply-labels).

## Verify

- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_issue_link.py -v` -- all cases green.
- Manually exercise the CLI against the live repo with a PR body that references a known issue:
  - `PR_BODY="Refs #123" python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo tvna/claude-md` exits 0 and prints `OK: #123 resolves in tvna/claude-md.`
  - `PR_BODY="" python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo tvna/claude-md` exits 1 with the no-ref error.
  - `PR_BODY="Refs #999999" python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo tvna/claude-md` exits 1 with the missing-ref error.
- Confirm the existing `Verify issue link` workflow runs green on the PR that lands this refactor (self-verification).

## References

- Parent: #123.
- Precedent: #112 -> #118 + #122 (`scripts/uv_pin.py`, `tests/test_uv_pin.py`).
- Origin issue for the workflow: #110.
- CLAUDE.md section 3 (deterministic harness) and section 4 (fail loudly, no silent defaults).

Sub-issue of #136 (P1, highest blast radius). Parent threat model: #102.

## Problem (fact)

`scripts/scan_non_ascii.py` line 137 returns `block` for any author
whose `author_association` is not `OWNER` / `MEMBER` / `COLLABORATOR`,
ignoring the `` opt-out. `dependabot[bot]`
reports `author_association: NONE` and routinely pastes upstream
release notes that contain zero-width spaces around `@mentions`. PR
#119 was therefore blocked and labeled `severity:non-ascii-content`
on a routine `actions/checkout` bump.

The workflow's only existing bot exemption is
`.github/workflows/scan-non-ascii.yml:26`
(`if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'`), which exists purely
to break the comment retrigger loop and does not generalize.

## Change

1. In `scripts/scan_non_ascii.py`:
   - Add `_TRUSTED_BOT_LOGINS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"dependabot[bot]"})`
     as a single source of truth (so future bots are a one-line add).
   - Thread the actor login into `classify_action` (currently it only
     receives `association`). The event payload already exposes it
     via `pull_request.user.login` / `issue.user.login` / `sender.login`
     depending on event type — pick the right field per the existing
     event-routing code.
   - When the login is in `_TRUSTED_BOT_LOGINS`, treat the actor as
     `trusted` for the `block` decision **only**. Still detect, still
     post the escaped-form advisory comment.

2. Do **not** suppress the scan itself, do **not** suppress the
   advisory comment, do **not** remove the `severity:non-ascii-content`
   label. Per #136 threat-model note: upstream release notes flowing
   into Claude sessions via `subscribe_pr_activity` remain the
   prompt-injection carrier — operators must still see the escaped
   form. The exception only removes the false `block`.

3. Add pytest cases in `tests/test_scan_non_ascii.py`:
   - `dependabot[bot]` + non-ASCII -> `advisory` (not `block`).
   - `dependabot[bot]` + ASCII-only -> `none`.
   - Unknown bot login (`renovate[bot]`) + non-ASCII -> `block`
     (allowlist is exact-match, no wildcard).
   - Existing trusted/external truth-table cases continue to pass.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_scan_non_ascii.py` green.
- Re-run the scan locally against the PR #119 event payload (replay
  via `python3 scripts/scan_non_ascii.py run` with a fixture) and
  confirm the comment posts but the action is `advisory`, not
  `block`.
- After merge, the next Dependabot PR opens without the
  `severity:non-ascii-content` block path, but the advisory comment
  still appears.

## Out of scope

- Renovate or other bot ecosystems (extend `_TRUSTED_BOT_LOGINS`
  when needed; not now).
- Removing the `severity:non-ascii-content` label on Dependabot PRs
  (keep it — it remains the operator's visual signal).
- Refactoring the workflow trigger filter (`if:` on line 26).

Sub-issue of #136 (P3). Related: #110 (the gate this issue carves an
exception out of).

## Problem (fact)

`.github/workflows/verify-issue-link.yml` plus
`scripts/issue_link.py` require every PR body to cite
`Refs #` / `Closes #` / `Fixes #` / `Resolves #`. The gate is listed
as a required status check in `.github/rulesets/main.json` lines
38-39. Dependabot PR bodies (PR #119 reproducer) never carry an
issue reference because they are not authored against an issue;
Dependabot spawns them on its own schedule.

Today, every Dependabot PR will fail this required check and become
unmergeable.

## Change

In `scripts/issue_link.py`:

- Read the PR author login from the event payload
  (`pull_request.user.login`).
- If the login is in the trusted-bot allowlist, exit `0` with a
  short stdout note (`skipped: trusted bot author`) and skip the
  `Refs #` regex check.
- Source the allowlist from the same `_TRUSTED_BOT_LOGINS` constant
  introduced in the P1 sub-issue (do **not** duplicate the bot
  login between scripts — that was the explicit non-goal stated in
  #136). If P1 hasn't merged yet, define the constant in a small
  shared module (`scripts/_trusted_bots.py`) that both scripts
  import.

Add a pytest case in `tests/test_issue_link.py`:

- `dependabot[bot]` author + no `Refs #` -> `0` exit, stdout
  contains `skipped`.
- Non-bot author + no `Refs #` -> non-zero exit (existing behaviour
  preserved).
- Non-bot author + `Refs #136` -> `0` exit (existing behaviour
  preserved).
- Unknown bot login + no `Refs #` -> non-zero exit (allowlist is
  exact-match).

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_issue_link.py` green.
- Re-run the check locally against PR #119's body and confirm exit
  `0` with the skip note.
- After merge, the next Dependabot PR's `verify-issue-link` status
  check goes green without operator intervention.

## Out of scope

- Auto-merging Dependabot PRs once all checks pass.
- Loosening the gate for human contributors.
- Migrating the constant into a config file (a Python module is
  enough; keep it simple).

Refs #136, #110.

items.original:
Per CLAUDE.md §3: "After each merge, auto-open a retrospective issue -- make this deterministic, not operator-memory."

## Shipped

- Refs: issue #146, PR #147, merged as `4605f89` on `main`.
- `scripts/preflight_non_ascii.py` (Layer 2.5 PreToolUse hook) + 36 pytest cases.
- `.claude/settings.json` PreToolUse matcher for the 7 GitHub MCP write tools.
- `docs/non-ascii-defense.md` Layer 2.5 section.

## What worked

- **Re-use over re-implementation.** Importing `detect_non_ascii` / `has_ack_marker` / `escape_for_comment` from `scan_non_ascii` keeps Layer 2 and Layer 2.5 from drifting; one regex, one marker semantic, one escape format.
- **Documented opt-out as the soft path.** Offering `` (already supported server-side) as one of the two remediation options means OWNER posts in Japanese still flow through with a single retry, without requiring the user to abandon non-ASCII content.
- **Fail-open on hook error.** Any parse/shape error logs `::error::` to stderr and exits 0 with no decision -- a hook bug cannot wedge the session, and Layer 2 backstops.
- **Plan mode + AskUserQuestion.** Three pre-implementation questions (behavior / location / scope) eliminated rework -- the design landed on the first commit.

## Friction

- **Test bug round-trip.** The emoji surrogate-pair assertion was first written as `r"🎯" in reason` (literal emoji), which the escaped output correctly does not contain. One test-only retry was needed. Cheap, but a reminder that "raw vs escaped" comparisons need explicit `\uXXXX` literals.
- **No `type:retrospective` label exists.** This issue is filed under `type:tracking` + `layer:meta` as a workaround. See "Harness gap" below.

## Shipped

- Refs: issue #139 (P3 sub-issue of #136), PR #144, merged as `ce9935c` on `main`.
- `scripts/_trusted_bots.py` -- new single source of truth for `_TRUSTED_BOT_LOGINS`.
- `scripts/issue_link.py` -- `--author` / `$PR_AUTHOR` short-circuit: trusted bot login exits 0 with `skipped: trusted bot author ()` before the Refs regex or any `gh api` call.
- `scripts/scan_non_ascii.py` -- now imports `_TRUSTED_BOT_LOGINS` from the shared module (removed local definition introduced in #137).
- `.github/workflows/verify-issue-link.yml` -- forwards `github.event.pull_request.user.login` as `PR_AUTHOR` / `--author`.
- 7 new pytest cases in `TestTrustedBotAllowlist` (total: 234 -> 241).

## What worked

- **Shared module over cross-script import.** Asked up front (AskUserQuestion) whether to extract `_TRUSTED_BOT_LOGINS` to a new module or import it from `scan_non_ascii`. Picked extraction; avoids coupling two scripts with unrelated responsibilities and gives the umbrella #136 non-duplication non-goal a real home.
- **Short-circuit before `gh api`.** The bot-skip path returns 0 before `extract_refs` runs, so Dependabot bodies containing mid-line `#N` mentions (e.g. `Bumps foo from 1.0 to 1.1`) cannot trigger spurious `gh api` calls. Pinned by `test_bot_author_does_not_resolve_unverifiable_refs` (asserts `issue_exists` is never invoked).
- **Exact-match allowlist.** `renovate[bot]` etc. still fail the gate; pinned by `test_unknown_bot_no_refs_still_fails`. Matches the same exact-match contract as Layer 2 (#137).
- **Environment-var fallback.** `--author` falls back to `$PR_AUTHOR`, mirroring the existing `--body-file` / `$PR_BODY` contract. Tested with `test_author_from_env_var` and `test_empty_author_falls_through` (empty string must NOT match the allowlist).
- **End-to-end manual verification.** Ran the script with `dependabot[bot]` and `tvna` author inputs before pushing -- caught the contract before CI did.

## Friction

- **Retrospective creation is still not automated.** Same finding as #148. CLAUDE.md §3 explicitly says it should be deterministic, not operator-memory. The agent did it manually after the user reported the merge.
- **No `type:retrospective` label exists.** Filed under `type:tracking` + `layer:meta` + `layer:p3-harness` as a workaround (same as #148).
- **`verify-issue-link` is a required check listed in `.github/rulesets/main.json` lines 38-39.** No drift detection caught that the rule and the gate could be mutually unmergeable for Dependabot -- the bug only surfaced because PR #119 reproduced it. Worth considering a periodic "would a Dependabot PR pass all required checks?" smoke test.

## Harness gap (the deterministic-retrospective rule itself)

Carried verbatim from #148 because nothing has been built since:

The repo carries the rule "auto-open a retrospective issue" in three places (`CLAUDE.md` line 45, `AGENTS.md` line 44, `.apm/instructions/master.instructions.md` line 40) but no workflow implements it. Candidates for the implementation slot:

- A `pull_request` workflow that runs on `closed && merged`, parses `Refs #NN` from the PR body, and opens a retrospective issue with a templated body and the linking labels.
- A `type:retrospective` label added to `.github/labels.json` so retrospectives are filterable.

This is now the second retrospective opened manually (after #148). Suggest promoting the gap to its own tracking issue if not already filed.

## Follow-ups

- [ ] Live verification on the next Dependabot PR: confirm `verify-issue-link` reports `skipped: trusted bot author (dependabot[bot])` and exits 0 without operator intervention (per #139 verification step 3).
- [ ] Consider adding a CI smoke test that simulates a Dependabot PR body + author against `verify-issue-link` so future regressions surface before the next real bump.
- [ ] Address the harness gap above (deterministic retrospective creation).
- [ ] Re-evaluate the allowlist when adding a second bot (e.g. `renovate[bot]`, `pre-commit-ci[bot]`). Today the constant lives in `scripts/_trusted_bots.py` and is already shared between Layer 2 (#137) and Layer P3 (#139); a third site would justify lifting it into config.

## Goal

Make threat-intelligence triage a sustained repository activity based on external collection, not just issue/PR metadata keywords.

## Current status

- PR #171 now collects external intelligence from OSV.dev for locked repository dependencies.
- PR #171 fetches CISA KEV and escalates OSV findings whose IDs or aliases are known exploited CVEs.
- The workflow applies `threat:intel-needed` for any repository-relevant external finding and `threat:response-needed` for KEV-correlated findings.
- Tests use OSV/CISA-shaped fixtures so deterministic gates do not require live network access.

## Sub-issues

- #172 — Query GitHub Advisory Database directly.
- #173 — Add EPSS exploit-likelihood enrichment.
- #174 — Add NVD CVE metadata enrichment.
- #175 — Monitor open-source malicious package intelligence.
- #176 — Extract GitHub Actions and transient dependencies.
- #177 — Define threat-intelligence source policy.

## Ongoing operating loop

1. Reconcile the new `threat:*` labels into GitHub using the existing label SoT/apply workflow.
2. Land the external threat-intelligence triage workflow and keep it covered by pytest.
3. Periodically review true positives, false positives, stale-label removals, and source coverage.
4. Consider additional external sources later, such as GitHub Security Advisories, ecosystem-specific advisories, and Dependabot/security alerts, after OSV/CISA are stable.
5. Document response handoff expectations before allowing autonomous fixes on security-sensitive work.

## Completion checks

- `python3 -m pytest` passes.
- `.github/labels.json` validates through `scripts/labels_apply.py validate`.
- The live GitHub label set includes `threat:intel-needed` and `threat:response-needed`.
- A fixture or live scan with an OSV dependency finding receives `threat:intel-needed`.
- A fixture or live scan with an OSV finding that aliases a CISA KEV CVE receives `threat:response-needed`.
- Sub-issues #172 through #177 are resolved or explicitly parked with rationale.

Refs #171

## Summary

Based on a CLAUDE.md revision proposal from a separate session, merged using the following three criteria.

1. **Prioritize Claude as the reader** — Remove descriptions that are self-evident to Claude
2. **Preserve strong wording** — Avoid paraphrasings that weaken normativity
3. **Strengthen rules by separation** — Keep merged rules split

## Changes adopted from the proposal

- **S3 Deterministic examples**: Removed 6 items that are self-evident to Claude
  - Removed: Formatting / Linting / Type checking / Unit tests / Build steps / Static analysis
  - Kept: Dependency resolution / Code generation / File renaming / Secret scanning
- **S3 wording compression**: `pull requests` → `PRs`, `if no such mechanism exists, establish` → `if missing, build`, `Assemble expert AI agents at a single point in the workflow` → `Concentrate expert agents at one workflow point`
- **S5 Skills and sub-agents description**: merged into a single line (`Use Skills (main-context workflows) for procedures, not sub-agents (isolated roles).`)
- **S6**: `Explain the trade-offs clearly so users can keep up with the reasoning.` → `Explain trade-offs so users follow the reasoning.`

## Points reverted from the proposal

- **Preserving strong wording** (criterion 2)
  - `actively use nix, uv, and microsoft/apm` (keep `actively use` and the `microsoft/` qualifier)
  - `prevent drift and defend against supply-chain attacks` (keep the double verb `prevent ... defend against`)
  - `degrades quality and creates inconsistency` (restored `inconsistency`, which the proposal had dropped)
  - `hooks, pre-commit, and CI/CD` (reverted the proposal's `CI` back to `CI/CD`)
- **Preserving separation** (criterion 3)
  - Keep S5 `Don't improve adjacent code, comments, or formatting.` and `Don't refactor things that aren't broken.` as 2 separate rules
  - Keep the 3-rule separation for agent task division in S5 (separation of implementation/verification, `Never let one agent review or test what it wrote.`, exploration agents are read-only, write-capable agents are limited to implementation steps)

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify the diff is as intended with `git diff main..HEAD -- CLAUDE.md`
- [ ] Render CLAUDE.md and verify the 6-section structure is preserved
- [ ] Verify §S3 Deterministic examples has 4 items
- [ ] Verify the number of rules under §S5 "When editing existing code" and "When delegating to sub-agents" remains the same as before

- Rewrote **body sections** (Purpose / The Six Principles / Using This From Another Project / Change Policy) in English.
- The **6-principle table summaries** are not direct translations — replaced with natural English one-liners.

Closes #14

Rewrite the opening bullet of Principle 3 as an imperative rule: open a GitHub issue before creating a branch, commit, or PR, and reference its number in every commit message and PR description. No exceptions, so trivial fixes (typos, docs, hotfixes) cannot silently route around the harness Principle 3 builds on.

The previous wording described where artifacts live; it lacked temporal force, so agents kept skipping issue creation. The new text subsumes that mapping while adding the missing ordering.

### Diff (the relevant bullet)

**Before:**
```
- Keep changes in git, proposals and issues in issues, and apply implementation through PRs.
```

**After:**
```
- Open a GitHub issue BEFORE creating a branch, commit, or PR, and reference its number in every commit message and PR description. No exceptions — typos, docs, and hotfixes included.
```

### Note (self-referential)

The change to this rule itself predates the rule's own merge and is the only exception. Issue #14 was opened after the PR was created, and is linked here retroactively.

## Summary

Resolves [#11](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/issues/11) and folds in two recurrence-prevention measures so the entire concern lands atomically.

The issue's "invalid syntax" premise turned out to be outdated: `exclude-newer = "14 days"` is valid in **uv ≥ 0.9.17** ([astral-sh/uv#16814](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/16814), Dec 9 2025). The reporter observed the warning on uv 0.8.17, which is below `required-version`. The real defects were (a) two sources of truth for the `14 days` value (pyproject.toml **and** the workflow CLI flag **and** README) and (b) no PR-time gate to catch regenerated-instruction drift.

## Changes

- **`generate-agents.yml`** — drop the redundant `--exclude-newer "14 days"` CLI flag; add `workflow_call` trigger with a `mode` input (`generate` default opens a PR on diff; `verify` fails on diff). PR-open step now gates on `inputs.mode != 'verify'`.
- **`verify-agents.yml`** *(new)* — pull-request trigger that calls `generate-agents.yml` with `mode: verify`. Paths filter restricts runs to PRs that can affect compile output. Permissions narrowed to read-only.
- **`pyproject.toml`** — raise `required-version` from `>=0.9.17` to `>=0.11.8` (the version that landed the sentinel-timestamp form for relative `exclude-newer`). Older uv versions emitting the warning class are now blocked outright.
- **`uv.lock`** — refreshed to the sentinel form (`exclude-newer-span = "P14D"`) so `uv sync --locked` stays clean under uv ≥ 0.11.8.
- **`README.md`** — drop the redundant CLI flag so the documented local command mirrors the workflow.

## Test plan

Locally (uv 0.11.11):

- [x] `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` on both workflows passes.
- [x] `uv sync --locked` is clean — no parse warnings.
- [x] `uv run --with "apm-cli==0.12.1" apm compile` produces no diff against committed `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`.
- [x] `uv` debug logs confirm `Solving with exclude-newer: global: <14-day sentinel>` for `--with` packages, proving `[tool.uv].exclude-newer` is honored after the CLI flag removal.

On PR open (GitHub-side):

- [ ] **`verify-agents.yml` job appears in the checks list** for this PR and passes (the drift gate verifies itself).
- [ ] If you intentionally edit `.apm/instructions/master.instructions.md` without re-running `apm compile`, the gate fails with the actionable error message (`Run 'uv sync --locked && uv run --with "apm-cli==0.12.1" apm compile' and commit the result.`).

## Out of scope

- `exclude-newer-package` per-package cooldown — user direction: handled via nix, tracked separately.
- Extracting `apm compile` into a shared shell script — user explicitly deferred (item 1 skipped); the `workflow_call` refactor already eliminates CI-side duplication.

Refs: #11

## Summary

Refs #18 Phase 0-B / Open Question #2.

Removes the `on.pull_request.paths` filter from `verify-agents.yml` so it triggers on every PR. To preserve the original "only do real work when APM-relevant files changed" semantics — and to ensure the future required status check (planned in #18 Phase 3-A) can never end up permanently `pending` on docs-only PRs — the single `verify` job is restructured into three jobs:

- **`detect`** — always runs; diffs PR head against base; emits `relevant=true|false` against the same file set the old path filter used (`.apm/**`, `apm.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `generate-agents.yml`, `verify-agents.yml`).
- **`verify`** — keeps the existing `workflow_call` into `generate-agents.yml` with `mode: verify`, gated on `needs.detect.outputs.relevant == 'true'`.
- **`gate`** — always-runs summary job; succeeds when there are no relevant changes OR when `verify` succeeded. This is the job intended to be promoted to a required status check in Phase 3-A.

No third-party actions added (per the precedent set in commit 8ce6796 "avoid third-party workflow actions"). The `actions/checkout` pin and `generate-agents.yml` semantics are unchanged.

> Note: this PR does **not** wire `verify-agents / gate` as a required status check — that is Phase 3-A.

## Test plan

- [ ] On this PR: `detect` runs and outputs `relevant=true` (this PR touches `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`). `verify` runs end-to-end. `gate` reports success.
- [ ] After merge, open a tiny docs-only follow-up PR (e.g. README typo): `detect` outputs `relevant=false`, `verify` is skipped, `gate` reports success.
- [ ] Open a PR that intentionally desyncs `CLAUDE.md`: `detect=true`, `verify` fails, `gate` reports failure with the surfaced result.

- Parent: #18 (Phase 0-B row of the [phased rollout comment](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/issues/18#issuecomment-4482593584))
- Resolves: Open Question #2 in #18
- Related: pre-existing `.github/workflows/verify-apm-drift.yml` (parallel drift workflow added in #12) is **not** touched here; cleanup left to a separate PR per CLAUDE.md §5 ("touch only what you must").

## Summary

Empty-commit PR to leave an application log of the Phase 2-A GUI operations (applying the `all-branches-no-force-push` ruleset + enabling "Automatically delete head branches"). Following the workflow in issue #27, squash-merging this PR engraves the apply history into the main history.

## Related Issue

Refs #27

## Changes

- Only 1 empty commit (`3b42e38b`). No code changes.
- The Phase 2-A application log is recorded in the body of this PR (see Verification below).

## Verification

### 1. Ruleset `all-branches-no-force-push`

Supporting comments:
[#issuecomment-4492278823](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/28#issuecomment-4492278823) (SoT crosscheck) /
[#issuecomment-4492325111](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/28#issuecomment-4492325111) (timestamps)

- [x] Ruleset id: `16562461`
- [x] Enforcement status: `Active`
- [x] Target: Include all branches + Exclude default branch
      (saved live as the `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` placeholder form, exactly matching the SoT)
- [x] Rules: only `Block force pushes` (`non_fast_forward`) is ON; `deletion` is not included
- [x] Bypass: `Repository admin` (Always)
- [x] Apply timestamp (UTC): `2026-05-18T23:40:07Z` (= ruleset `created_at`)
      Note: this is ~30 minutes ahead of issue #27 creation (`2026-05-19T00:10:17Z`). Since the SoT PR (#25) was already merged in advance, it is acceptable for Phase 2-A operations.

### 2. Auto-delete head branches

Supporting comment: [#issuecomment-4492302195](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/28#issuecomment-4492302195)

- [x] `Settings → General → Pull Requests → Automatically delete head branches` is ON
      (Repository API: `delete_branch_on_merge: true`)
- [x] Timestamp when set to ON (UTC): **n/a (cannot be retrieved retroactively)**
      — GitHub has no API to retrieve the timestamp of a Repository-settings toggle (Repo's `updated_at` also moves on other metadata updates), and the Audit log API is limited to Enterprise plans. The GUI Activity tab does not record repo-settings changes by design either.

### 3. Smoke test — force-push rejected (`docs/rulesets.md` §Verify item 2)

Supporting comments:
[#issuecomment-4492261104](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/28#issuecomment-4492261104) (Admin bypass observation) /
[#issuecomment-4492268961](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/28#issuecomment-4492268961) (cleanup observation) /
[#issuecomment-4492362524](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/28#issuecomment-4492362524) (**literal reject achieved**)

- [x] Result: **literal reject observed**
      Temporarily PUT `bypass_mode` from `"always"` → `"pull_request"`
      (drift window: `2026-05-19T21:50:40Z` to `2026-05-19T21:51:08Z`, about 28 seconds), then
      attempted `git push --force` as Admin (tvna). The following reject log was observed:

      ```
      remote: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/smoke/phase-2a-strict-1779227452.
      remote: - Cannot force-push to this branch
      ! [remote rejected] smoke/phase-2a-strict-1779227452 -> smoke/phase-2a-strict-1779227452 (push declined due to repository rule violations)
      ```

      After the test, restored `bypass_mode: "always"` and re-verified an exact match with the SoT ([#issuecomment-4492362524](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/28#issuecomment-4492362524) Step 4).

## Checklist

- [x] Issue number recorded on the `Refs #27` line above
- [x] CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md regenerated if applicable
      (this PR does not change `.apm/instructions/**`, so regeneration is not needed)
- [x] CI green — **N/A**: since this PR is an empty commit (zero diff), no checks run, including `paths`-constrained workflows. `required_status_checks` (`Verify agent instructions / gate`) is scheduled to be introduced after the `main.json` application in Phase 3-A (#18 rollout), so it is not a blocker for this PR under Phase 2-A.

## Summary

Expand `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` from the minimal `Summary` / `Test plan` form to the structure proposed in #29 (`Summary` / `Related Issue` / `Changes` / `Verification` / `Checklist`), and switch the default issue-reference placeholder to `Refs #` so squash commit bodies reliably contain `#\d+`.

This is Phase 0-A of the staged rollout in #18: it lands the template prerequisite **before** Phase 3-B activates `"commit_message_pattern": "#\\d+"` on `.github/rulesets/main.json`. Without this, merges to `main` would start being blocked once the rule turns on.

## Related Issue

Refs #29
Refs #18 (Phase 0-A)

## Changes

- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`: rewrite to the issue #29 structure; default placeholder is `Refs #` (avoids unintended auto-close on multi-issue PRs); update the HTML comment to explicitly call out the Phase 3-B regex so future editors don't strip the reference line.

## Verification

- [x] This PR's body itself follows the new template — `Refs #29` is present in the body, so the squash commit will contain `#\d+`.
- [x] Headings match issue #29's proposed structure 1:1 (English-only per repo convention, confirmed with the issue author).
- [ ] After squash merge: `git log -1 --format=%B origin/main` includes `#\d+` (issue #29 verification step 2 — to be confirmed by the merger).
- [ ] Required status check `Verify agent instructions / gate` is green (no change to `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, so the gate should pass without regeneration).

- [x] CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md regenerated if applicable — N/A, template is not part of generated agent instructions

- New `ISSUE_TEMPLATE` files (issue #29 only requests the PR template).

## Summary

Add `.github/labels.json` as the SoT, and align the inline values in the Apply / Update sections of `docs/ai-triage-routing.md` (already merged to main via #38) to be byte-for-byte identical with the SoT. Phase 2 of #34.

- `.github/labels.json` — 4 `agent:*` labels (`name` / `description` / `color`)
- `docs/ai-triage-routing.md` — Align `-f color=` / `-f description=` across the 4 Apply blocks + 1 Update block with the SoT, and remove the `(Phase 2 — not yet committed)` annotation

Actual label registration is an operator action after merge (same pattern as `docs/rulesets.md`; this PR does not run `gh api`).

## Related Issue

Refs #34
Closes #36

## Changes

- New `.github/labels.json` (22 lines)
- `docs/ai-triage-routing.md` patched in 5 places (12 lines / 24 changes)
  - Rewrite the opening lead's "not yet committed" mention into "SoT is committed in the same repo + must be byte-for-byte identical with the Apply section"
  - Remove the `*(Phase 2 — not yet committed)*` annotation in the SoT layout table
  - Align `color` / `description` of the 4 Apply blocks with the SoT
  - Sync the `agent:auto-fix` description in the Update example block as well
  - Remove the "Colour choices follow a traffic-light..." paragraph since the new palette breaks that intuition

## Trade-offs (Principle 6)

- **Registration is an operator action**: same flow as `docs/rulesets.md`. After merge, run the 4 Apply blocks from the runbook; close #36 once `gh api /repos/tvna/claude-md/labels` confirms 4 entries.
- **Rebase from a stale base**: this PR was opened on `43c92a0`, but main had advanced by 6 PRs since, so it was synced via `git rebase origin/main`. The original "main rewound by 6 PRs" theory is fully rejected.
- **Issue #35 is closed manually, separately**: Phase 1 landed on main via PR #38, but the commit message did not follow the `Closes #35` form, so auto-close did not fire. It will be closed manually, independently of this PR (and is not referenced in this PR body).

- [x] `python -m json.tool .github/labels.json` exits 0
- [x] The `name` / `description` / `color` triples in `.github/labels.json` exactly match the 4 blocks under §Apply in `docs/ai-triage-routing.md` (verified by grep)
- [x] The `agent:auto-fix` description in the §Update example block of `docs/ai-triage-routing.md` is also synced to the SoT (verified by grep)
- [ ] CI: non-firing via path filter works correctly
      (`verify-agents.yml` / `verify-apm-drift.yml` / `generate-agents.yml`
      all have trigger paths like `.apm/**` / `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`,
      none of which intersect with the paths changed in this PR)
- [ ] Reviewer check: the 4 `name` / `description` / `color` triples match between the runbook and the SoT

## Post-merge (operator action, out of scope for this PR)

1. Run the 4 blocks under §Apply in `docs/ai-triage-routing.md` in order
2. Confirm 4 entries with `gh api /repos/tvna/claude-md/labels --jq '.[] | select(.name | startswith("agent:")) | {name, color, description}'`
3. Close #36
4. (As a separate sub-issue under Phase 3) Retroactively apply `agent:*` to the 6 existing open issues

## Checklist

- [x] Issue number recorded on the `Refs #` / `Closes #` lines above
- [x] CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md regenerated if applicable
      (this PR does not change `.apm/instructions/**`, so regeneration is not needed)
- [ ] CI green (path filter not firing = expected)

## Summary

Updated project standards across AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and master.instructions.md to clarify key guidance on planning, error handling, agent delegation, and team empowerment. Changes emphasize the distinction between verification design and execution, proportional documentation, decision-making in error handling, and the proper use of Skills vs. sub-agents.

## Related Issue

Refs #45

## Changes

- **§1 (Plan Mode):** Clarified that plan mode should design verification steps, with execution delegated to separate agents (§5). Added guidance to match documentation weight to blast radius rather than always writing detailed PRDs.

- **§3 (Git Harness):** Added clarification that issue-first process and deterministic gates are overhead by design and don't violate §4's minimum-code rule, which scopes the change itself, not the process.

- **§4 (Simplicity & Safety):**
  - Reframed error handling guidance: "First decide whether a check is needed" before applying the impossible/plausible distinction.
  - Clarified "fail loudly" applies only when a check IS warranted, not universally.

- **§5 (Delegation):**
  - Replaced two separate bullet points with unified guidance: delegate to sub-agents when only the conclusion matters (tests, logs, searches); use Skills when the main context must follow steps in-line.
  - Clarified the roles: sub-agents isolate verbose work; Skills encode procedures for in-line execution.

- **§6 (Force Multiplier):** Reframed from "encourage people to go beyond human limitations" to "help people reach further than they could alone — and keep the decision theirs" to emphasize agency and shared ownership.

## Commits

### 1. `b0fb3b5` — replace gh CLI with curl (#53)

The first post-merge dispatch of `Apply rulesets` failed because the `gh` CLI was not available on the runner. Eliminate the dependency entirely by rewriting all 9 `gh api` call sites to use `curl + jq`, both of which are universally preinstalled on every linux runner.

Behavioral changes:
- GET sites use `curl --fail-with-body` so non-2xx responses still print the GitHub error body and propagate via `set -euo pipefail`.
- POST/PUT retry loop now captures HTTP status via `-w '%{http_code}'` and retries only on `>= 500` or curl-level failure (`000`). Previous code retried all failures, masking terminal 4xx validation errors.
- Auto-delete PATCH switches from `-F delete_branch_on_merge=true` form encoding to a `-d` JSON literal with `Content-Type: application/json`.

The job-level `GH_TOKEN` env stays as-is and is reused as the curl bearer token, so no change is required to the `RULESETS_PAT` secret.

### 2. `19bddc4` — drop bogus `/roles` pre-check that always 404s (#55)

Smoke-dispatching commit 1 from this branch surfaced a second defect inherited from #52: the `Pre-check admin role id matches bypass_actors` step calls `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/roles`, which **does not exist** as a GitHub REST API endpoint. Personal repositories have no "list custom repository roles" API at all — custom roles are org-only (`/orgs/{org}/custom-repository-roles`), and standard role IDs (1=Read, 2=Triage, 3=Write, 4=Maintain, 5=Admin) are documented constants. The `gh api` version was failing identically; the curl rewrite just made the failure visible.

Removed the entire step. The safety net is preserved at the apply call itself: a wrong actor_id makes POST/PUT return 422 with a structured error, which the existing error-surface code writes verbatim to the step summary.

## Verification

- `actionlint + shellcheck` (zero warnings)
- `grep -c "gh api"` → 0, `grep -c "/roles"` → 0
- YAML parser confirms 6 steps (down from 7; pre-check removed)
- External contract (workflow inputs, step summary table) unchanged

## Post-merge dispatch

1. Dispatch with `ruleset=both, dry_run=true, enable_auto_delete=false`
2. Expect: step summary "0 matches → plan-only (POST)" for both rulesets, no live changes
3. Proceed with Phase 2-A (`ruleset=all-branches, dry_run=false, enable_auto_delete=true`) → closes #27
4. Then Phase 3-A (`ruleset=main, dry_run=false`) → closes #41

## Closes

Closes #53, closes #55. Refs #51, #18, #27, #41.

## Summary

PR-1 of 3 under #56 (security hardening). Adds two reinforcing defenses against `RULESETS_PAT` exfiltration via malicious workflow body on a feature branch:

1. **`environment: ruleset-apply`** on the `apply` job. Secret resolution requires GitHub Environment configuration (required reviewer + branch policy restricted to `main`). Dispatch from any non-`main` ref cannot load the secret; even main dispatches pause for human approval before any step runs.
2. **`Guard dispatch ref` (new first step)** — fail-fast with `::error::` when `github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'`. Belt-and-suspenders for Environment misconfiguration; verifiable on this PR branch itself.

## Why both

The job-level `env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RULESETS_PAT }}` interpolates the secret into every step's env at job start. An attacker who modifies any step in a feature branch (including the ref-guard step) can read `$GH_TOKEN` **before the `if:` evaluates** — so the ref guard alone is insufficient. The Environment-scoped secret is the actual primary defense (the secret is simply not available off the allowed branches); the ref guard prevents accidental cross-branch dispatch and protects against env misconfiguration.

## ⚠️ Operator pre-conditions (MUST complete BEFORE merging this PR)

1. GitHub UI → **Settings → Environments → New environment** named **exactly** `ruleset-apply`.
2. In that environment:
   - **Required reviewers** = `@tvna`
   - **Wait timer** = 0
   - **Deployment branch policy** = "Selected branches and tags" → add `main` only
3. In that environment: **Add secret** `RULESETS_PAT` with the **same** fine-grained PAT value currently stored at repo level.
4. **Do NOT delete the repo-level `RULESETS_PAT` yet** — keep it as rollback insurance until this PR merges and one successful post-merge dispatch confirms the env-scoped secret resolves. Then delete the repo-level one.

## Verification

- ✅ `actionlint -shellcheck=shellcheck` clean
- ✅ YAML parses (`python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"`)
- ✅ Diff: +7 lines, no removals, two surgical changes
- **Pre-merge smoke (do this on this PR branch)**: dispatch `Apply rulesets` against `claude/issue-56-env-gate-apply-rulesets`. Must fail at the very first step `Guard dispatch ref` with `::error::apply-rulesets must be dispatched against main (got refs/heads/claude/issue-56-env-gate-apply-rulesets).` *before any subsequent step runs and before `$GH_TOKEN` is ever needed*. This confirms the ref-guard wiring without requiring the Environment.
- **Post-merge**: dispatch against `main` with `ruleset=both, dry_run=true`. Must pause with "Waiting for review" in the Environments UI before any step runs. Approve → job proceeds → step summary should look identical to a dry-run on the previous workflow body.

## Diff

```yaml
 jobs:
   apply:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment: ruleset-apply
     steps:
+      - name: Guard dispatch ref
+        if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'
+        run: |
+          echo "::error::apply-rulesets must be dispatched against main (got ${{ github.ref }})."
+          exit 1
+
       - name: Guard RULESETS_PAT
```

## Rollback

`git revert` this commit. Environment secret remains usable by the reverted workflow body if the operator hasn't yet deleted the repo-level secret (per pre-condition #4). If they have, restore the repo-level secret first.

## Follow-ups under #56

- **PR-2**: `.github/CODEOWNERS` (P1-a)
- **PR-3**: `require_code_owner_review: true` on `main.json` + `docs/rulesets.md` updates (P1-b + P1-c + P2-a + P2-b)

Refs #18, #51, #56.

## Summary

Closes #64.

`verify-agents.yml` calls `generate-agents.yml` as a reusable workflow with `mode: verify` and granted only `contents: read` / `pull-requests: read` to the `verify` job. The callee declares `contents: write` / `pull-requests: write` at the top level, so GitHub Actions rejected the call at parse time for any PR touching APM-relevant paths.

### Why not Option B (the "cleaner" option in the issue body)

I first tried Option B (top-level `read` + job-level `write` in `generate-agents.yml`). It does **not** work — GitHub Actions validates job-level permission declarations of the callee against the caller's grants at parse time too, not only top-level. The error simply shifted:

- Before: `The workflow is requesting 'contents: write, pull-requests: write'`
- After Option B attempt: `The nested job 'generate' is requesting 'contents: write, pull-requests: write'`

Issue #64's pitfall note that "Top-level `read` + job-level `write` works" was inaccurate for the `workflow_call` case.

### Fix — Option A

Raise the `verify-agents.yml` `verify` job grants to match the callee's top-level declaration. The PR-creation step in `generate-agents.yml` is gated by `if: ${{ inputs.mode != 'verify' }}`, so the write grant on the verify caller is **inert in practice** — verify mode only executes the read-only drift check (`git diff`).

```diff
 # verify-agents.yml
   verify:
     uses: ./.github/workflows/generate-agents.yml
     with:
       mode: verify
     permissions:
-      contents: read
-      pull-requests: read
+      contents: write
```

## Summary

Closes #64.

`verify-agents.yml` calls `generate-agents.yml` as a reusable workflow with `mode: verify` and granted only `contents: read` / `pull-requests: read` to the `verify` job. The callee declares `contents: write` / `pull-requests: write` at the top level, so GitHub Actions rejected the call at parse time for any PR touching APM-relevant paths.

### Why not Option B (the "cleaner" option in the issue body)

I first tried Option B (top-level `read` + job-level `write` in `generate-agents.yml`). It does **not** work -- GitHub Actions validates job-level permission declarations of the callee against the caller's grants at parse time too, not only top-level. The error simply shifted:

- Before: `The workflow is requesting 'contents: write, pull-requests: write'`
- After Option B attempt: `The nested job 'generate' is requesting 'contents: write, pull-requests: write'`

Issue #64's pitfall note that "Top-level `read` + job-level `write` works" was inaccurate for the `workflow_call` case.

### Fix -- Option A

Raise the `verify-agents.yml` `verify` job grants to match the callee's top-level declaration. The PR-creation step in `generate-agents.yml` is gated by `if: ${{ inputs.mode != 'verify' }}`, so the write grant on the verify caller is **inert in practice** -- verify mode only executes the read-only drift check (`git diff`).

```diff

   verify:
     uses: ./.github/workflows/generate-agents.yml
     with:
       mode: verify
     permissions:
-      contents: read
-      pull-requests: read
+      contents: write
+      pull-requests: write
```

#56 PR-3 of 3. Lands the remaining tamper-resistance items so that the very rulesets being rolled out cannot be bypassed during their own rollout.

| Item | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| **P1-b** | `.github/rulesets/main.json` | Flip `require_code_owner_review` from `false` to `true`. |
| **P1-c** | `docs/rulesets.md` Phase mapping | Annotate the 3-A row so it is clear P1-b ships inside the same PUT as the rest of `main.json` (no extra dispatch). |
| **P2-a** | `docs/rulesets.md` | New `## Dispatch authorization criteria` section: linked open Phase issue, ignore comment-only requests, `dry_run=true` first, + prompt-injection callout for PR-activity-subscribed Claude sessions. |
| **P2-b** | `docs/rulesets.md` §Verify | New `### Post-apply audit log review` subsection enumerating the `repository_ruleset.*` and `environment.deployment_approval` audit-log entries to inspect after every apply. |

## Why now

PR-2 (#66) landed the `CODEOWNERS` file in advisory mode. This PR is the second half: enabling `require_code_owner_review: true` so that the next Phase 3-A (#41) dispatch activates the enforcement at the same time as the rest of `main.json` (one PUT, not two). ```

```
PR-3 (this PR)     ─ main.json require_code_owner_review + docs (P1-b/c, P2-a/b)
```

Refs #18, #56.

## Summary

Adds a one-line `*Layer: ...*` italic subtitle to each of the six principles in `.apm/instructions/master.instructions.md`, so chapter interactions become structural rather than disclaimer-based. README "Six Principles" tables (EN + JP) gain a Layer column. CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md regenerated.

| § | Layer |
|---|---|
| 1 | goal & plan structure |
| 2 | pre-code reasoning |
| 3 | delivery harness around the code (not artifact code itself) |
| 4 | artifact code |
| 5 | change scope & agent split |
| 6 | handoff & communication |

After this change, the §3-vs-§4 conflict that the previously removed disclaimer addressed ("process overhead, not artifact code") is ruled out by construction: §3 declares its layer as *delivery harness*, §4 declares its layer as *artifact code*. Different layers cannot conflict by construction; no cross-chapter exception links are needed.

The one remaining cross-reference inside §3 (`§2 applies: failure output and review text are the spec — fix the loop.`) is kept deliberately — it represents *layer cooperation*, not conflict. See the review comment in this PR for the full deliberation.

Closes #75.

The §2/§3 reframe and the LLM-wording tighten work tracked under #73 landed earlier via #74. This PR is the structural follow-up to that work and was originally bundled with it; after #74 merged, the branch was rebased onto main so this PR now carries only the Layer identifier change.

Closes #77.

## Summary

Move the debug-logging rule out of §5 (`Accelerate Scale with Quality` → `When editing existing code`) and into §4 (`Simplicity, Bounded by Safety`) with explicit threat-model wording.

## Why

The original bullet — `If you receive a bug report or fix request, use restricted-access debug logs.` — had three weaknesses for LLM interpretation:

1. **Ambiguous noun phrase** — "restricted-access debug logs" reads as either "logs gated by access control" (output sink) or "logs of restricted-access information" (content). Neither maps cleanly to the actual intent (preventing credential leakage and protecting layers whose security depends on obscurity).
2. **Wrong Layer** — sat in §5 (scope discipline) but the purpose is harm prevention. Per the Layer identifiers added in #75/#76, §4 (`artifact code — what prevents harm`) is the correct home.
3. **Trigger too narrow** — gated on "bug report or fix request," but the leak risk applies to any diagnostic instrumentation, not just bug-fix flows.

## What changed

- **§4** (`.apm/instructions/master.instructions.md`): new bullet inserted between `Keep confirmations and dry-runs...` and `When a check IS warranted, fail loudly...`:
  > Treat debug instrumentation as an attack surface. Redact credentials, tokens, and PII before logging, and route diagnostic output to an access-controlled sink — never widen exposure to chase a bug.
- **§5**: the ambiguous bullet is deleted from the `When editing existing code` block.
- `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`: regenerated mechanically via `apm compile`.
- `README.md`: unchanged. Both `Six Principles` table summaries for §4 and §5 still fit; only an internal bullet moves.

## Spec coverage

| Original intent | New §4 bullet |
|----|----|
| Prevent credential leakage during debug | `Redact credentials, tokens, and PII before logging` |
| Protect security-by-obscurity layers (attack surface) | `Treat debug instrumentation as an attack surface` + `never widen exposure to chase a bug` |
| Access-controlled diagnostic output | `route diagnostic output to an access-controlled sink` |

No spec dropped. Trigger is intentionally widened — the threat applies to all diagnostic instrumentation, not only bug-fix flows.

## Out of scope (explicit decisions)

- No cleanup clause (e.g. `remove after the bug is closed`) — §5's `orphans` block already covers self-cleanup in general; adding a debug-log-specific cleanup would duplicate it.
- No `README.md` row update — titles and summaries for §4/§5 are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [ ] `git diff origin/main -- .apm/instructions/master.instructions.md` shows exactly +1 line in §4 and -1 line in §5.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` regenerated diffs reflect the same structural delta (plus build-ID bump).
- [ ] `README.md` and `uv.lock` are unchanged.
- [ ] §4 reads naturally with the new bullet between `confirmations/dry-runs` and `fail loudly`.
- [ ] §5 `When editing existing code` reads as a coherent scope-discipline list after the removal.

## Summary

Reposition the §5 closing verification rule to §1, then reframe it as a plan-time specification rule (not an execution-time gate) to match §1's planning character. Resolves Issue #79's F2; F5 (sub-block structure) intentionally deferred with justification below.

## Related Issue

Refs #79

## Why Option C, with reframe

Per Issue #79, four candidate directions remained viable after Option D (new §7) was ruled out by the DoD line "no README row changes required". Option C chosen on **Layer purity** — the closing rule's substance is verification, which matches §1's Layer string (*"goal & plan structure — what the work is and how it will be verified"*).

**Reframe rationale** (added in second commit after initial review): the moved paragraph in its original imperative form ("Before declaring a task complete, you must prove it works...") read as an execution-time gate dropped into a planning chapter — Layer-correct by literal wording but tonally mismatched with §1's planning character (stepwise decomposition toward the goal). The reframe folds the substance into bullet 3 as a **plan-time specification rule**:

- Goal decomposition into ordered steps (planning verb)
- Per-step traceability to a user requirement
- Per-step completion check (tests / logs / UI / scripts)
- Anti-pattern preserved: type checks and linters verify shape, not behavior
- Escape hatch preserved: environment-can't-run → say so in the plan

The execution-time "definition of done" imperative is replaced structurally: §1 *specifies* completion checks, §5's `Split implementation and verification across separate agents` *executes* them.

## Changes

- **`.apm/instructions/master.instructions.md`**
  - §1 bullet 3 (extended): "Design verification in the plan (execution belongs to a separate agent). **Decompose the goal into ordered steps; each step traces to a user requirement and declares its own completion check — running the tests, checking the logs, exercising UI flows, running scripts/APIs end-to-end. Type checks and linters verify code shape, not behavior. When the environment cannot run the check, say so in the plan up front — never let indirect signals stand in for proof.**"
  - §1 bullet 3's old tail split into a new bullet 4: "Match the document weight to the blast radius: detailed PRD for architectural / multi-PR work, concise spec otherwise."
  - §1 returns to flat-bullet style with no closing paragraph (matches §2/§3/§5/§6).
  - §5: closing paragraph deleted. §5 now ends with the last bullet of `When delegating to sub-agents:` (`Split implementation and verification across separate agents...`).
  - Cross-ref `— see §5` trimmed from §1 bullet 3's parenthetical; `(execution belongs to a separate agent)` retained as a lightweight cooperation pointer to §5's agent-split rule.
- **`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`**: regenerated mechanically via `uv run --with "apm-cli==0.12.1" apm compile`. Byte-identical between consecutive compiles (Build-ID is deterministic when source content is unchanged).
- **`README.md` / `apm.yml`**: unchanged. Both "Six Principles" tables (EN + JP) still hold — §1's row summary "goal & plan structure" and §5's row summary "change scope & agent split" do not move.

## F5 disposition (sub-block structure)

**Kept as-is, with justification.** Issue #79's DoD requires §5 structure to be "internally consistent (sub-blocks either justified or removed)". The three sub-blocks (`When editing existing code:`, `When your changes create orphans:`, `When delegating to sub-agents:`) delineate **functionally orthogonal scenarios**:

- Editing-existing-code rules (don't refactor adjacent / match style / leave dead code) do not apply when delegating to sub-agents.
- Orphan-cleanup rules apply only to code your own changes made unused.
- Sub-agent-delegation rules govern when to use Skills vs. sub-agents and how to split implementation/verification.

Flattening these into a single bullet list would force each bullet to re-state its scenario context, inflating the chapter without adding signal. The named sub-block headers act as scenario gates that prevent rule misapplication.

If reviewers disagree, F5 should spin out as a follow-up issue rather than expand this PR's scope.

- [x] `git diff origin/main -- .apm/instructions/master.instructions.md` shows: §1 bullet 3 expanded + new §1 bullet 4 (doc-weight split out) + §5 closing paragraph removed.
- [x] `uv run --with "apm-cli==0.12.1" apm compile` regenerates `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` without errors.
- [x] Second `apm compile` is byte-identical to the first (md5 confirmed); the drift gate in `.github/workflows/verify-apm-drift.yml` will pass.
- [x] `git diff origin/main -- README.md apm.yml` is empty.
- [x] §1 is back to a flat-bullet style with no closing paragraph (consistent with §2/§3/§5/§6).
- [x] §5 still has its three sub-blocks; ending with `Split implementation and verification across separate agents...` reads as a natural close to `When delegating to sub-agents:`.

## Summary

Followup to merged PR #81. During post-merge review of #81, it was pointed out that `.claudeignore` was treated as the authoritative "Claude tooling" SoT in `docs/repo-scope.md` without a primary source. Primary-source verification ([#58 comment](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/issues/58#issuecomment-4502888322)) found that the [Claude Code Settings page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) only documents `respectGitignore` for the `@` file picker — `.claudeignore` is **not** a documented Claude Code primitive.

Per the post-merge decision, the `.claudeignore` file is kept (historical state + forward-looking convention), but `docs/repo-scope.md` now explicitly records that `.gitignore` is the canonical enforcement and `.claudeignore` is a courtesy mirror whose original framing in #81 was hallucination-derived.

## Related Issue

Refs #60
Refs #58

## Changes

- `docs/repo-scope.md` SoT layout table — downgraded `.claudeignore` row: `Target` now reads "no official Claude Code support — see *Note on `.claudeignore`* below"; `Purpose` reads "Forward-looking mirror, kept on speculation. Not authoritative." The `.gitignore` row is annotated as the source of truth.
- New section *Note on `.claudeignore` — kept as speculation, not as an official primitive* — cites the Claude Code Settings docs (only `respectGitignore` is documented), cites The Register's 2026-01-28 reporting that `.claudeignore` is not reliably honoured, lists the two reasons the file is kept (historical state from `f513b88`; forward-looking convention), and links to the [#58 comment](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/issues/58#issuecomment-4502888322) so the original hallucination finding survives in tree.
- *References* expanded with the Claude Code Settings docs link and the #58 comment.

No code change to `.gitignore` or `.claudeignore`. The 9 prohibited patterns added in #81 stay in place.

## Verification

- [x] `git diff origin/main..HEAD -- docs/repo-scope.md` shows only the documentation change (no `.gitignore` / `.claudeignore` diff).
- [x] No changes to `.apm/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `apm.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, or `uv.lock` — `verify-apm-drift` / `verify-agents` will short-circuit on the `detect` job.
- [x] The hallucination acknowledgement is concentrated in a single named section (*Note on `.claudeignore`*) so future readers landing via `git blame` or grep find it deterministically.

- [x] Issue number recorded on the `Refs #` line above
- [x] CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md regenerated if applicable *(N/A — only `docs/`)*
- [ ] CI green
